title: Bob Stoops: Hired in 1998, OU's All-Time Wins Leader
question: When was Bob Stoops hired at Oklahoma and how many games did he win?
answer: Oklahoma hired Bob Stoops on Dec. 1, 1998, from Florida, where he was defensive coordinator. He went 190-48 from 1999 to 2016, the most wins in OU history, and passed Barry Switzer's 157 on Nov. 23, 2013, at Kansas State.
summary: OU hired Bob Stoops on Dec. 1, 1998. He went 190-48 over 18 seasons, passing Barry Switzer in 2013 to become the program's all-time wins leader.
body: The hire that changed modern Oklahoma football happened on Dec. 1, 1998. Athletic director Joe Castiglione, running the search himself, landed Bob Stoops, a former Iowa safety who had been Steve Spurrier's defensive coordinator at Florida. Stoops was hired one day before Kirk Ferentz got the Iowa job, and he took over a program coming off three straight losing seasons.

The turnaround was immediate, and the consistency was remarkable. In 18 seasons from 1999 to 2016, Stoops went 190-48, a .798 winning percentage, and 121-29 in Big 12 play. His teams won 10 Big 12 championships, posted 14 seasons with double-digit wins, never had a losing season and went 9-9 in bowl games. He also won the 2000 national title and coached Heisman winners Jason White and Sam Bradford.
The program wins record fell on Nov. 23, 2013, when the Sooners won 41-27 on the road at Kansas State. That victory pushed Stoops past Barry Switzer's 157 wins for the most in school history.

Stoops retired on June 7, 2017, handing the job to 33-year-old Lincoln Riley. He briefly returned as interim coach for OU's bowl game after the 2021 season and won it, which is why some OU sources list his total as 191-48. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him with its 2021 class, and its bio notes he is the only coach to win a national title plus all four BCS bowls.
